where: Section 1, the 'where' line under the formula
problem: The unit 'in rad/s' is attached to the gain: '|G(jω)| is the gain at frequency ω in rad/s'. Gain is not measured in rad/s; rad/s belongs to the frequency ω. A student may copy the wrong unit into an answer.
fix: '|G(jω)| is the gain at that frequency (dimensionless when G is a plain gain); ω is the frequency in rad/s, and ∠G(jω) is the phase in degrees or radians.'

where: Section 2, start of the fourth paragraph
problem: 'For a proper system, the magnitude at ω→∞ is 0' is not true for all proper systems. A proper system with as many zeros as poles (m=n) ends at a finite non-zero magnitude; only a strictly proper system (m<n) ends at 0. The very next line uses the no-zero case, so the loose word can confuse.
fix: 'For a strictly proper system (more poles than zeros, m<n), the magnitude at ω→∞ is 0.'
